title: Wrong-person first-failure transition is not taken_over_at-guarded at the UPDATE — a take-over landing between the token lookup and the transition yanks a landlord-handled row into awaiting_correction (r2 blocker pattern, residual TOCTOU)
evidence: form_handler.gleam:1235 'case row.taken_over_at != "" { True -> wisp.redirect(to: "/reference/" <> token) False -> ... case row.correction_cycles >= 1 { True -> exhaust_wrong_person(config, row, id_uuid, token) False -> ... sql.update_reference_call_status(config.db, id_uuid, sql.AwaitingCorrection, "", "contact_invalid", sql.ContactInitiated)' — update_reference_call_status.sql: 'WHERE id = $1 AND status = $5::reference_call_status' (no taken_over_at filter) — contrast mark_awaiting_correction.sql:23 'AND taken_over_at IS NULL' and sweep_claim_t0.sql 'r1 (N12): a take-over landing between the due-SELECT and the send must not be followed by a T0 invite — the landlord is handling it (A7). AND taken_over_at IS NULL'
detail: The cycles>=1 wrong-person leg exhausts via exhaust_reference_call (guarded), but the first-failure leg relies solely on the pre-read row.taken_over_at check. A take-over committing between lookup_context and the UPDATE lets a wrong-person POST transition a landlord-handled row to awaiting_correction — the exact r2-blocker outcome; a later correct then leaves the row queued+taken-over, which the sweep excludes forever (no re-invite) and correction clears the form token, dead-ending §8.6.
recommended_fix: Give the wrong-person first-failure leg a dedicated guarded transition (WHERE id=$1 AND status='contact_initiated' AND taken_over_at IS NULL), mirroring mark_awaiting_correction.sql; a 0-row result redirects to the token's truthful state as the existing 0-row arm does.
